title: Delta Ledger + Approval Tokens (PRD sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is an early PRD sketch for a lightweight, network-friendly audit ledger ("Delta Ledger") plus short-lived cryptographic approval tokens to record and validate customer-managed network changes in private deployments. Goal: provide traceable change records and verifiable approvals while minimizing bandwidth and storage impact for constrained customer edges (NATed, low-bandwidth, air-gapped).

Why this is different / problem statement:
- Many customers run the private control plane behind customer-managed networking (NAT, strict egress) and want tamper-resilient change history for networking/admin changes without shipping full verbose logs offsite.
- Existing approaches either send full event dumps (high bandwidth, privacy concerns) or only summarize (loses recoverability for investigations).
- We need a middle path: small, reconstructable deltas + verifiable approval receipts that are tamper-evident and respect customer retention/consent policies.

Goals (measurable):
- Keep typical per-change outbound payload < 1.2 KB after compression for small changes.
- Provide 3 reconstructability tiers (full, reconstructable-deltas, digest-only) selectable per-tenant.
- Approval token issuance and verification latency < 300 ms in normal hosted flows; acceptable offline issuance for air-gapped connectors (signed token files).
- End-to-end cryptographic linkage so ledger tampering is detectable even if full event body is not shipped.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We are not replacing full compliance-grade long-term retention; this complements existing long-retention pipelines for enterprise customers.
- Not a replacement for SIEM integration; but should make integration simpler via compact artifacts or periodic full exports.
- Must work across deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem).

Design overview (high level):
1) Delta Ledger concept:
   - Per-tenant append-only sequence of change deltas (sequence_id, time, actor, delta-type, compact-payload-hash, optional encrypted payload reference).
   - Each delta includes a small metadata vector (operation, impacted objects, severity, optional human comment) and a cryptographic digest (SHA-256) of the full change payload.
   - For privacy, full payloads are optional: tenant can choose to keep full payload locally and only send digest/delta upstream.
   - Ledger entries are chained via a rolling-accumulator (not full blockchain): H_n = H(H_{n-1} || entry_n_digest). This makes contiguous tampering detectable.

2) Approval Tokens:
   - When an approver (console/API/operator) approves a change, system emits an Approval Token tied to ledger sequence numbers affected.
   - Token is a compact signed object: {tenant_id, seq_start, seq_end, approver_id, action, ttl, token_sig}
   - Default token TTL is short (minutes) for interactive flows. For scheduled change windows, tokens can be pre-signed with additional metadata.
   - Tokens are signed by Redwood's signing key by default; for customers with HSM/KMS we support customer-supplied signing keys (optional).

3) Data flow / connectors:
   - Edge connector (lightweight binary/agent) accumulates local deltas and maintains local ledger state.
   - Connectors ship either: streaming (mTLS) to the designated ingestion endpoint, or periodic bundles (signed rollup files) for offline/air-gapped upload.
   - Bundles contain: manifest (sequence ranges), compressed delta array, ledger checkpoint signature, and optional encrypted full payload archive (if tenant opted in).
   - For customers with strict egress, connector supports a push-to-S3 or push-to-carrier approach (SFTP) and an offline handoff process.

4) Reconstructability tiers (tenant selection):
   - Full: full payloads + ledger entries in cloud. Default for enterprise retention customers.
   - Reconstructable-deltas: compact deltas + enough metadata to reconstruct intent (actions, objects, hashes). Certain fields redacted for PII.
   - Digest-only: minimum leakage — only sequence + digest chain + approval tokens retained. Useful for privacy-sensitive customers.

API sketches (surface-level):
   - POST /v1/deltas/submit -> {seq_range_ack, ingest_token}
   - GET /v1/ledger/checkpoint?tenant_id= -> {last_seq, H_last}
   - POST /v1/approvals/issue -> {approval_token}
   - POST /v1/bundles/upload -> {bundle_id, validate_report}
   - POST /v1/approvals/verify -> {valid: true|false, reason}
Notes: exact shapes TBD. Tokens are compact base64 JSON with signature.

Security model and keys:
   - Support Redwood-managed signing keys by default (rotated quarterly).
   - Optional: customer-supplied derived signing keys (KMS/HSM) for approval token signing.
   - Ledger chaining prevents suffix tampering; we also include periodic signed checkpoints anchored to a customer-provided key for extra non-repudiation.
   - TLS + mTLS for connector traffic. Signed bundles for offline transfers.

Observability and SLOs:
   - Metrics: deltas/sec, avg bytes/delta, bundle-latency, token-issue-latency, token-verify-latency, reconcile-failures.
   - Alerts: bundle-skip-rate > 1% on connectors, ledger-gap detected, token verification failures.

Failure modes / mitigations:
   - Connector offline for extended period -> local journal grows; limit size + rotation + operator alert. Encourage periodic signed bundle export.
   - Sequence gaps on ingest -> accept out-of-order but mark gaps, request replay of missing seq ranges. Support partial ingestion with gap markers.
   - Approval token signature key compromise -> revoke via revocation table and re-sign affected checkpoints; we expose revocation-list endpoint.

Privacy and compliance notes:
   - Tenant-level retention policy determines how long full payloads vs digests are stored.
   - Offer an automated purge tool and TTL enforcement.
   - Allow data residency control: ledger checkpoint records can be stored in region X while full payloads stay customer-side.

UX/Console implications (rough):
   - Console: show compact change stream with expand-to-fetch-full-payload (if tenant stored full payloads in-cloud).
   - Approval flow: issue ephemeral token at approval time; UI shows token validity and sequence range it covers.
   - Troubleshooting: link from token to bundle(s) and connector IDs for investigators.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
   1) Internal alpha: SDK + connector changes behind feature flag; Redwood-managed keys only. (Q1)
   2) Beta with select customers (Dedicated + Private) supporting offline bundles. (Q2)
   3) Customer-key signing + console integration (Q3)
   4) GA with retention tiers and integration guides (Q4)

Open questions / TODOs:
   - How big should the canonical delta schema be? (TODO: create compact schema proposal, link JIRA PD-2253)
   - Decide on default digest algorithm and checkpoint cadence.
   - UX: approval token revocation UX and audit trail visibility.
   - Legal: confirm that digest-only mode satisfies typical compliance needs for SOC2/ISO; involve security/compliance team.

Next steps (immediate):
   - Draft compact delta schema (owner: Priya) -> due 2025-11-20. (JIRA: PD-2253)
   - Spike: connector bundle format + signing (owner: Ethan) -> due 2 weeks.
   - Security sync to define key management options (owner: Lucas) -> schedule this week.

Notes / rough links:
   - Related: CONFLUENCE PD-1128 (private logging options), JIRA PD-2217 (connector push work), GH repo: network-connector#42 (bundle prototype)

Random early UX ideas (brainstorm):
   - "Approval token mini-QR" that operator can copy into change ticket for cross-validation.
   - "Gap detective": small tool that solicits signed replay from connectors when ledger gap found and attempts automated reconciliation.

Quick risks to call out:
   - Risk: Customers expect full fidelity for investigations; need clear contract that digest-only tier trades fidelity for privacy and cost.
   - Risk: Key management complexity if we offer customer-supplied signing — must be opinionated and well-documented.

End of sketch. This is intentionally lightweight — want feedback on core tradeoffs (bandwidth vs reconstructability, verification model, and offline handoff UX).
notes: TODOs inline: PD-2253 schema, connector bundle spike, security sync. Slack thread: #private-deploy-approval. Will refine after spike results.
short_summary: PRD sketch proposing a Delta Ledger (compact per-change deltas + chained digests) and short-lived Approval Tokens to provide verifiable, low-bandwidth audit and approval recording for customer-managed networks in private deployments.
